web_evidence.title: Apples Never Fall — Macmillan
web_evidence.note: The publisher's sustained Chapter 1 excerpt narrates the siblings and waitress externally, including the waitress's perceptions and thoughts, in third person.

web_evidence.title: Apples Never Fall Book Club Kit
web_evidence.note: Macmillan's official whole-book guide explicitly says the story is told in third person through the major characters' eyes in turn and across two timelines.

web_evidence.title: Liane Moriarty Writing Styles in Apples Never Fall
web_evidence.note: The study guide explicitly identifies third-person narration from the main characters' respective points of view.

web_evidence.title: Apples Never Fall Literary Devices
web_evidence.note: The structural analysis describes chapters rotating among characters' limited perspectives and explicitly distinguishes the design from first-person narration.

person_note: The controlling narration is third person with rotating close or limited focalization across Joy, Stan, their children, and minor observers, plus shifts between timelines. The numerous sustained quote passages that refer to focal characters as she, he, or they while rendering their private thoughts agree with the authorized opening and Macmillan's explicit whole-book description. First-person and second-person forms in the quote set occur in dialogue, direct thought, memories, or universal maxims, not sustained base sections, so multiple viewpoints do not make the book ALTERNATING. A few clipped passages remain locally unclear, but no credible evidence conflicts with the third-person structure.
